title: XLE FWD
infotainment: Toyota Audio Multimedia, 12.3-inch touchscreen, cloud-based navigation, OTA updates, 6 USB-C ports.
adasStandard: Toyota Safety Sense 3.0: Pre-Collision System with Pedestrian Detection, Full-Speed Range Dynamic Radar Cruise Control, Lane Departure Alert with Steering Assist, Lane Tracing Assist, Automatic High Beams, Road Sign Assist, Proactive Driving Assist. Source: https://www.toyota.com/safety-sense/animation/tss3
adasOptional: Blind Spot Monitor with Rear Cross-Traffic Alert (standard on XLE). Traffic Jam Assist (hands-on, low-speed) standard. Source: https://www.toyota.com/bz4x/features/
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard rear-view backup camera with dynamic guidelines. Source: https://www.toyota.com/bz4x/features/
sideViewCameraNotes: Panoramic View Monitor (360-degree camera) optional via Premium package on XLE. Source: https://www.toyota.com/bz4x/features/
subscriptionFeatures: Remote Connect (remote start via app/key fob): 10-year trial then $80/yr or $8/mo. Drive Connect (cloud nav): 1-year trial then $200/yr. Wi-Fi Connect hotspot: 1 month / 3GB trial then plans from $25/mo. Safety Connect: 10-year trial then $80/yr. Source: https://www.toyota.com/connected-services/
drmNotes: Vehicle operates fully without cellular connectivity. Toyota Connected Services (Remote Connect, Service Connect, Safety Connect, Wi-Fi Connect, Drive Connect) bundled trials of 3-10 years vary by feature; renewals are subscription-based. Toyota Audio Multimedia infotainment functions locally. Source: https://www.toyota.com/connected-services/
killSwitchNotes: No impaired-driving-detection kill switch on MY2025. Toyota has not announced specific implementation for the IIJA federal mandate. Source: https://www.dadss.org/
knownIssues: Slow DC fast charging in cold weather widely reported (battery thermal management lacks active heating for charging). One-pedal driving mode does not fully stop the vehicle. 12V battery drain issues reported on early units. Source: https://www.bz4xforum.com/ ; https://insideevs.com/news/620521/toyota-bz4x-cold-weather-charging-issues/
recalls: NHTSA 22V-460 (June 2022): wheel hub bolt loosening, potential wheel detachment, stop-sale until remediated. Resolved on current production. Source: https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls (campaign 22V-460)
stateIncentives: Toyota bZ4X is assembled in Japan and does not qualify for the federal IRA $7,500 clean vehicle credit (final assembly requirement). May qualify for $4,000 used credit after first sale. State incentives vary: CA CVRP up to $2,000 (income-eligible, available while funded); CO $5,000; CT $2,250; MA MOR-EV $3,500; NJ sales-tax exempt; NY $2,000. Source: https://fueleconomy.gov/feg/tax2023.shtml ; https://afdc.energy.gov/laws/state
tcoSource: Edmunds True Cost to Own for 2025 Toyota bZ4X XLE (Edmunds reports the same per-cost-bucket breakdown across XLE FWD/AWD variants of the 2025 bZ4X). 5-year totals at 15,000 mi/yr; ownership costs exclude any Federal EV Tax Credit. Source: https://www.edmunds.com/toyota/bz4x/2025/cost-to-own/
